chunks: And it was also narrated from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Isma'il ibn Jabir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The time for prayer enters upon me while I am traveling, so I do not pray until I enter to my family.' He said: 'Pray and complete the prayer.' I said: 'The time for prayer enters upon me while I am with my family, desiring to travel, so I do not pray until I leave.' He said: 'Then pray and shorten (the prayer), and if you do not do so, by Allah, you have opposed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer when traveling if prayer time begins while still at home?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal criterion for *Qasr* (shortening) versus *Tamam* (completing) prayer based on the traveler's status at the onset of prayer time. It establishes that if one is already in the state of travel when the time enters, the full four-rak'ah prayer is performed; conversely, if one is at home and intends to depart, the prayer must be shortened. The Imam’s warning that failing to shorten in the latter case constitutes opposing the Prophet underscores the binding nature of this distinction in Shia jurisprudence.
